Mark face $i$ as visible if $v_i > 0$ [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that a face is marked as visible if its normal vector component in the viewing direction ($v_i$) is positive. The evidence in Source [S2] explains that back-face culling involves a 'simple dot product between the face normal and the viewing direction' and is used to avoid rendering geometry that 'faces away from the user'. In standard computer graphics, a face is considered front-facing (and thus visible) if the dot product of its normal and the view direction is positive (assuming the normal points outward and the view direction points from the eye to the object, or vice versa depending on convention, but the sign determines visibility). The evidence confirms the mechanism (dot product) and the purpose (culling back faces), which aligns with the mathematical condition described in the claim.
